THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.
The proceedings which have been initiated against the husband and two others are the subject matter of this criminal petition.

The police registered an FIR for the offenses punishable under Section 498A of the IPC which ultimately culminated in filling of a charge sheet and the husband alone is before this Court challenging the same.

2. Learned counsel appearing for the wife-second respondent files an affidavit which reads follows:
"HEREIN, I D.S.Vidyasree Daughter of Srinivasa, Aged about 30 years, residing at Doddadasarahalli village, Kasaba Hobli, Sidlaghatta taluk, Chikkaballapura dist now at Sidlaghatta do hereby NC: 2024:KHC:21070 state on solemn affirmation and swear to this Affidavit as under.
1. I am the respondent No: 2 in the top noted case.
I know the facts and circumstances of the case.
Hence, competent to swear to this Affidavit.

2. the Petitioner has filed the top noted Petition being aggrieved by the order of taking cognizance of the offence punishable under Sections 498(A) Of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and praying for quashing of all the further proceedings in Criminal Case No:916/2017 (Sidlaghatta RURAL Police Station Crime No: 296/2017) pending on the files of the learned Principal Civil Judge and Judicial Magistrate First Class,
Sidlaghatta.

sentences.text: I have no any objection to allow the petition and quash the entire proceedings in the above referred case pending before the principal civil judge at Sidlaghatta in C.C.No.916/2017.

I may be permitted to file of necessary petition of dissolution NC:
2024:KHC:21070 of marriage before the jurisdictional Court by mutual consent of the petitioner.
6. I undertake that I will not file any cases before any court of law against petitioner herein.

WHEREFORE, I the respondent No.2 most humbly pray that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to allow the petition filled by the petitioner and quash the entire proceedings, in the interest of justice".
3.

The second respondent is also personally present in this Court and she states that she has no objections for quashing of the proceedings and that she does not intend to prosecute the case against her husband and is willing to lead a life without any litigation.

4. Having regard to the fact that the dispute is essentially private in nature and the wife has settled her differences with her husband by stating that she intends to file a petition for dissolution of marriage, in my view, this would be an appropriate case to compound the offenses and quash the entire proceedings.

Since the wife is NC: 2024:KHC:21070 categorically stating that she is not interested in prosecuting the proceedings, notwithstanding the fact that the other accused have not challenged the proceedings, in the interest of justice, it would be appropriate quash the entire proceedings.
Consequently, the proceedings pending before the Principal Civil Judge and Judicial Magistrate First Class, Sidlaghatta shall stand quashed.

5. The Criminal Petition is accordingly allowed.
Sd/-
